definitions.explanation: A central virtue in Confucian ethics, representing kindness, compassion, and love toward others. One of the five Confucian virtues and a fundamental concept in East Asian moral philosophy.

examples.japanese: {仁|じん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{儒教|じゅきょう}→儒教：11530_jukyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{根本|こんぽん}→根本：13107_konpon⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦{徳|とく}→徳：23014_toku⟧だ。
examples.english: Benevolence is the foundational virtue of Confucianism.

examples.japanese: ⟦{孔子|こうし}→孔子：26143_koushi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{弟子|でし}→弟子：03986_deshi⟧たち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{仁|じん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧さ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{繰|く}り{返|かえ}し→繰り返す：02051_kurikaesu⟧⟦{説|と}いた→説く：14245_toku⟧。
examples.english: Confucius repeatedly taught his disciples the importance of benevolence.

notes:
One of the five Confucian virtues ({五常|ごじょう}), {仁|じん} is considered the highest and most encompassing. It represents the ideal of treating others with genuine compassion and care. In Japanese culture, this concept deeply influenced samurai ethics (⟦{武士道|ぶしどう}→武士道：17460_bushidou⟧) and remains a respected ideal.

THE FIVE CONFUCIAN VIRTUES ({五常|ごじょう}):
- {仁|じん}: benevolence
- {義|ぎ}: righteousness
- ⟦{礼|れい}→礼：02170_rei⟧: propriety
- {智|ち}: wisdom
- {信|しん}: faithfulness

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仁|じん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{心|こころ}→心：01321_kokoro⟧: a benevolent heart
- {仁|じん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{施|ほどこ}す→施す：12985_hodokosu⟧: to bestow benevolence
- {仁愛|じんあい}: benevolent love, compassion
- {仁義|じんぎ}: benevolence and righteousness; also honor code (in yakuza contexts)
- {仁徳|じんとく}: virtuous benevolence

USAGE:
Also used as a male given name ({仁|じん} or {仁|ひとし}). Not to be confused with the suffix ⟦{人|じん}→〜人：09849_jin⟧ (person), which is a different character.
